ships.name: Korbatar Makwar
ships.description: One of the last great Korath battleships from the height of the war that drove their species to near extinction, the Korbatar Makwar is an engine of destruction that dominates conventional battlefields. 	The number of these battleships which are still in operation can be counted on one hand. Korath shipyards are fully capable of assembling more Korbatar Makwars, but the exile from Korath space has forced them to prioritize construction of Korsmanath A'awojs and other support vessels instead. A small, but vocal, group of Navarchs continue to lobby various planning committees for construction of new Korbatar Makwars. But the civilian government refuses to capitulate to their demands.

ships.name: Modified Cargo Star
ships.description: The Cargo Star was a proprietary freighter used by Starwell Shipping Corporation before it was bought out by the Syndicate in a hostile corporate takeover. Many of the technologies and design principles from this ship can be found in the modern designs of Syndicate Shipyards. 	Most Cargo Stars that survived the Alpha Wars did so by having extensive modifications made to strengthen their hull, shields, and weapon capacity.

variants.name: Korsmanath A'awoj (Refiner)
variants.description: Korsmanath A'awojs, named in memory of the Korath home system, are massive nomadic habitats that hold much of their remaining population. True flying cities, they could be self-contained miniature worlds were it not for their heavy defensive armament and reliance on unsustainable materials, methods, and sources of power. 	Commission of new Korsmanath A'awojs is a resource-demanding, labor-intensive, painstaking process fraught with political intrigue. Navarchs fight with the civilian government for resources and yard time they would rather devote to building raiding and defensive fleets, civilians vie with each other for a place on the next ship, and planning committees argue with engineers over what methods and technologies to use. This leads to construction delays, corner-cutting, and over-militarization of the design at best, and violent feuds at worst.

variants.description: The Avialae is an early example of Remnant ship development. Its design function still has traces of principles from ancestral human space. As they acclimated to life in the Ember Wastes many Prefects determined that mass production of big Utility ships was a waste of resources. variants.name: Korbatar Makwar (Exile Upgrade)
variants.description: One of the last great Korath battleships from the height of the war that drove their species to near extinction, the Korbatar Makwar is an engine of destruction that dominates conventional battlefields. 	The number of these battleships which are still in operation can be counted on one hand. Korath shipyards are fully capable of assembling more Korbatar Makwars, but the exile from Korath space has forced them to prioritize construction of Korsmanath A'awojs and other support vessels instead. A small, but vocal, group of Navarchs continue to lobby various planning committees for construction of new Korbatar Makwars. But the civilian government refuses to capitulate to their demands.

variants.description: Shortly after development of the Starling, Remnant ship crafters attempted to apply the design principles they learned towards a medium warship. outfits.name: Quantum Drive (Damaged)
outfits.description: The Quantum Drive allows travel to any point in time and space... When it's working properly. This damaged Quantum Drive still makes it possible to travel over distances beyond what can be achieved with a regular Jump Drive.

outfits.name: Electron Ion Turret
outfits.description: The internal diagnostic program indicates that it is a Tarazed test model prototype. But all of the listed log entries are in the future instead of the past.

outfits.name: Heavy Double Anti-Missile
outfits.description: A few customers have expressed an interest in buying a Heavy Double Anti-Missile Turret in the past. But in market research surveys it has never beaten demand for some form of Particle Turret.

outfits.name: Refurbished Fusion Cannon
outfits.description: There is an old faded piece of paper attached to the targeting control panel: 	"We've done our best to restore this old Prototype Fusion Cannon to a functional state. I'm glad I was able to end my career on a high note. Make sure you come back from this mission in one piece. You won't want to miss my retirement party!" - Barmy

outfits.name: Quantum Torpedo
outfits.description: Quantum Torpedoes are ammunition for the Quantum Torpedo Launcher. Each Quantum Torpedo Launcher can hold 30 of them. You cannot install torpedoes unless you have also installed a launcher to fire them from.

outfits.name: Quantum Torpedo Rack
outfits.description: The Quantum Torpedo Storage Rack is used to store extra ammunition for Quantum Torpedo Launchers.

outfits.name: Quantum Torpedo Depot
outfits.description: The Quantum Torpedo Storage Depot stages extra ammunition in your cargo bay for weapons that use Quantum Torpedoes. The ammunition is ready to be withdrawn for use. Storing it this way uses more cargo space than if it were packed away in sealed crates. An extra crewmember is required to maintain inventory.

outfits.name: Quantum Torpedo Launcher
outfits.description: Quantum Torpedoes are able to quantum shift though obstacles that block line of sight to the target. This effect also negates anti-missile defenses and penetrates shields. The manufacturer is unknown.

outfits.name: Quantum Torpedo Pod
outfits.description: Quantum Torpedoes are able to quantum shift though obstacles that block line of sight to the target. This effect also negates anti-missile defenses and penetrates shields. The manufacturer is unknown. 	Pods enable fighters and other light craft to carry small quantities of Torpedoes into battle while retaining enough space for other weapons. Large ships are better off with full-size launchers.

outfits.name: Vacuum Ramscoop
outfits.description: This Vacuum Ramscoop aggressively collects fuel from the solar wind, but loses power and generates heat while it does so. Though it appears to be a product of Deep Sky, none of their outfitters recognize it.

outfits.name: Modified S-270 Regenerator
outfits.description: This modified S-270 regenerator restores shields more quickly but drains more energy and runs hotter than the standard version.

outfits.name: Modified S-970 Regenerator
outfits.description: This modified S-970 regenerator restores shields more quickly but drains more energy and runs hotter than the standard version.

outfits.name: S-KR53 Hull Repair System
outfits.description: This hull repair system from Syndicate Systems is more advanced than anything in their catalogue and should be a top seller. Strangely, any Syndicate sales representative who is asked about this product claims it doesn't exist.

outfits.name: North Wind Helium
outfits.description: While bulkier than the industry standard Liquid Helium Cooler, this new system offers additional emergency cooling if the ship starts to overheat.

outfits.name: Apocalypse Core
outfits.description: This appears to be a collaboration between Lovelace Labs and Turner Inc. However, this product does not appear in either company's catalogue.

outfits.name: A510 Atomic Engines
outfits.description: This compact steering and thrusting engine isn't as efficient as separate atomic thruster and steering engines of similar size. But using this can free up a considerable amount of space for other outfits or weapons. It seems like this should be a popular product, but Deep Sky outfitters have never heard of it.

outfits.name: Scattershot Depot

outfits.name: Scattershot Gun
outfits.description: The Scattershot Gun racks shells that split into multiple shots which spread out to cover a wide area. The loading systems on them are less likely to jam compared to species that put more resources on developing their energy weapons.

outfits.name: Shock Wave Blaster

The ionized plasma fired from these weapons is composed of charged particles that are extremely volatile. They lose cohesion after only a short distance of flight, making them less accurate against distant targets.

description.text: The Syndicate has a generous vacation policy on Foundry that allows workers to take as much as a month of vacation time every year, and many choose to take that time to escape from the cities and explore the wilderness. The shipyards claim that this vacation time is partly responsible for the high reliability of the ships built here, because a well-rested and relaxed worker is less likely to make the sort of mistakes that can quickly become disastrous in outer space.

spaceport.text: Everything is made of gleaming metal, and each tower is slightly tapered and adorned with painted fins that make it resemble an enormous starship.

values: Foundry is home to Syndicated Shipyards, where more than half of the commercial freighters in human space are manufactured. Although much of the planet is blanketed in smog from the factories, there are also regions of pristine forests and majestic mountains.

The spaceport is surrounded by kilometers of hangars and factories where new ships are being assembled.

The port itself is a trio of towering buildings, with a skywalk on the top floors to provide a view of the surrounding area. Larger ships land on pads around the base of the towers, while smaller ships can fly into hangars built into the sides of the towers themselves.
Everything is made of gleaming metal, and each tower is slightly tapered and adorned with painted fins that make it resemble an enormous starship.

description.text: Stormhold is a cold planet, with a dense, foggy atmosphere. As with many pirate outposts, Stormhold is home to an unknown number of villages and hidden outposts, each controlled by a different pirate faction. It is also said that some of the most dangerous fugitives in the galaxy live deep in the forests of this planet, escaping detection by living underground or by avoiding the use of electronic devices.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is a large town, with a population of roughly thirty thousand. People of all races and cultures mingle freely, while keeping a wary eye open for off-worlders who may be Republic agents in disguise.

description.text: One island archipelago is home to the spaceport, the only part of the planet where it is safe to land uninvited. The other islands - even some that seem from a distance to be uninhabited - are often used as staging bases for pirate fleets, who guard their secrets closely.

spaceport.text: Your ship is on a landing pad only a few meters above the pounding surf, and you can't help worrying about what might happen if the tide rises any higher. If nothing else, the salt water is bound to corrode your hull if you stay here too long. You make your way to a bar where a cage hanging from the ceiling holds an actual parrot. After trying for a while to get it to talk to you, you realize that it is dead, stuffed and nailed to its perch.

values: Deadman's Cove is an ocean planet; the continents take up only a tenth of its surface area. Legends tell of massive sea creatures hiding in the deeps: serpents hundreds of meters long; colossal sea turtles; strange tentacled monsters and exotic fish.

description.text: All the industry on Nimbus is driven by the sea. Fish are plentiful, and the oceans here also contain some unique microorganisms that are harvested to extract useful medical compounds.

spaceport.text: Thankfully the weather is warm, but you are glad to find a cozy, dry, and welcoming space in the coffeehouse across from the warehouse district.

values: Nimbus is a stormy ocean world, where a rain shower can descend on you almost without warning, only to be replaced with equal suddenness by bright sunshine. It draws mostly the sort of people who can weather such changes with placid, unperturbed calm; tourist guidebooks often rank Nimbus near the top in their lists of "friendliest natives."

description.text: At present, Seraglio is the focus of considerable attention from researchers searching for clues as to the planet's history.

values: Seraglio's vast ice fields hint at a variety of mysteries, most notably the chasms that suggest the planet was somehow subjected to massive compressive forces at some point in its recent geological history.
At present, Seraglio is the focus of considerable attention from researchers searching for clues as to the planet's history.

description.text: At present, Babiali has a regular stream of mining and research craft systematically flying over the crust looking for rare metals or anything else of value. Despite the activity, no one has bothered to set up anything resembling a spaceport.

values: Babiali's surface is a bona fide example of cataclysm. Ice and rock extends from horizon to horizon, with vast networks of cracks and fissures suggesting it was subject to some kind of sudden force fairly recently in its geological history.

At present, Babiali has a regular stream of mining and research craft systematically flying over the crust looking for rare metals or anything else of value. Despite the activity, no one has bothered to set up anything resembling a spaceport.

description.text: Eminonu's notably green rocks show a remarkably high copper content and the historic presence of atmospheric water. Scattered vegetative debris suggests that this world was, until recently, some variety of garden planet, albeit likely a cold one. Today the vast majority of moisture is locked up in ice fields, and the ambient temperatures are far too cold for even hardy lichens to survive.

values: While this moon's minerals aren't particularly rare or exotic, its closeness to Viminal has made it the subject of many mining projects over the centuries - efforts to find traces of the valuable Key Stones which permit travel through this region of space. None of them were successful, and most Remnant scientists believe that Kumkapi formed somewhere else and was captured by Viminal's gravitational pull at some time during its formation.

description.text: This cold and dreary world would certainly not be attractive to any modern settlers, but to those who were fleeing the chaos of the Alpha Wars it had the undeniable advantage of being isolated and undiscovered. The continued Remnant presence here is due to the planet's Key Stones, which enable ships to travel through certain wormholes in the Ember Waste, and which the Remnant have not found on any other planet.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is an enormous dome, built of the same resilient and semi-organic material as the hulls of Remnant ships. An opening at one end of the dome allows ships to fly in and out. Inside, the air is still cold, but at least you are sheltered from the violent winds that sweep across the rest of the planet's surface. Some of the locals, accustomed to the cold, walk about in their shirtsleeves as if this were a balmy summer day.

values: Much like Aksaray, Topkapi is an old moon formed from the smashed remains of countless eons worth of stellar debris. The surface appears to be regularly bombarded by asteroids, although some of the craters show signs of being the site of rather large explosions. Your sensors pick up traces of materials most commonly found in Korath ships.

description.text: A brief consultation of your navigational computer's economic database, however, indicates that all the minerals present in this variant of regolith are very common across the galaxy and have an extremely low value.

values: At first glance, Aksaray appears to be a fairly generic moon formed from eons of dust and debris compressed into a tight ball by constant gravitational pressure. What is not commonplace is the presence of almost perfectly pyramidal piles of regolith scattered across the world. Querying an orbiting Remnant satellite suggests that these are believed to have been remote mining sites for mineral processing.

A brief consultation of your navigational computer's economic database, however, indicates that all the minerals present in this variant of regolith are very common across the galaxy and have an extremely low value.

description.text: While virtually every craft that tries to land here is a fuel scooping drone, a large number of satellites orbit Yedikule at various heights, meaning that it must have been exhaustively studied in the past.

values: Although much smaller than most gaseous planets - including the one it orbits - the thick atmosphere of Yedikule and its rocky core make it a gas dwarf. While it was not the first to be discovered in human history, it is very improbable to have formed around a gas giant, and the extreme differences between its atmosphere and the one of Xerolophos further suggest this was not its original location.

description.text: While it's possible that Xerolophos might have migrated here long ago, the Remnant haven't been able to explain the extreme temperatures of the planet even after years of studies and dispatching dozens of probes.

values: Although formerly classified as a "Hot Jupiter," Xerolophos does not present all the characteristics of one: it is very far from the system star - so distant that it isn't even tidally locked to it. Its temperature, instead, is unusually high even for a Hot Jupiter, with the core internally heating up the atmosphere much more than expected.

While it's possible that Xerolophos might have migrated here long ago, the Remnant haven't been able to explain the extreme temperatures of the planet even after years of studies and dispatching dozens of probes.

description.text: Tibernia is a classic ice planet, but unlike most, it is nearly a perfect sphere with a remarkably smooth surface blemished by few craters. Many have speculated that it is artificial, but so far no one has found conclusive evidence of this.

description.text: When the first members of the Remnant discovered this region of space, Caelian was the only habitable world they found with enough insolation to be able to operate solar-powered factories and bioreactors. The first settlements were scattered widely, with the houses hidden underground in order to be less visible from space, because they feared that the Alphas would overrun human space and eventually find their way into the Waste. Centuries later, when they learned that the Alpha Wars had ended, they began to expand the factories and settlements more openly.

spaceport.text: Nearly all members of the Remnant are dark-skinned, either from exposure to high levels of ultraviolet radiation or because that is what their first ancestors who came here looked like. So, they walk around this spaceport village without much fear of the scorching desert sun, bringing supplies back and forth to the houses and to the flat clay pavement of the landing zone. Aside from some camels that the settlers brought with them, there are very few animals here.

Why they would be concerned with the geological formations of an uninhabited planet is unknown, but the research continues.

values: Pincian is a small rocky moon, tiny enough to avoid most asteroids attracted by the nearby gas giant of Palatine. Nevertheless, a huge crater, old enough to have collected some dust and regolith, dominates its surface. Whatever crashed here, it must be tens of thousands of years since the impact.

description.text: Over the subsequent centuries the winds have been imperceptibly slowing toward normally predicted velocities, but at their current rate it will be many millennia before they reach them.

values: The whipping winds of Palatine are a prime example of how the inner mechanics of gas giants are poorly understood; when it was initially discovered by the Remnant, its winds spun around the globe at speeds far in excess of what astrophysical models predicted, as if they had recently been subject to a massive acceleration.

description.text: One of the smallest "Hot Jupiters" known, Baliesa is a calm, undemanding gas giant. Occasional storms form near the terminator line between the night and day side, but soon split into smaller and smaller vortexes until they disappear. The violet-tinted skies of the upper atmosphere leave space to a bright pink-colored haze below, hampering visual navigation but otherwise not causing any trouble.

The Syndicate often destroys pirate factories at their borders, but their fleets do not find the monetary cost of venturing as far as New Tortuga worth the benefit. Here, shipyards, factories, and outfitters provide a continuous supply of goods and services for the system.

The most significant settlements on the planet are built predominantly underground, far from any fault lines, with only obscure, hardened access areas. Combined with the fortress-like blast doors that blockade the spaceport entrances, New Tortuga is the perfect place for those looking for somewhere to hide.

As a result, the surface is of comparatively recent origin. Despite this, you can spot a small survey station in the middle of an old lava field. In response to your landing computer's query, the transponder issues a terse statement about the automated scientific station and a warning that its defense systems are active.

description.text: This is not a particularly warm world, but it is the best that the first Remnant refugees were able to find when they explored the Ember Waste. It is here that they built their capital, in a deep valley that is almost always shrouded in clouds. In meadows farther up the mountain slopes, a few particularly hardy food crops are grown, but for the most part the Remnant rely on artificial greenhouses or cultured yeast for protein supplements. Remnant cuisine is unlikely to ever become a draw for tourists, even if their isolation here is broken.

spaceport.text: The oldest buildings in the Remnant capital city harken back to classic human architecture, with stone facades and columns reminiscent of ancient Rome. But as you walk outward toward the more recent additions, the buildings become less and less recognizably human, with curved organic shapes and hundreds of overhanging walkways and balconies. It is as if the layers left behind by centuries of habitation are a frozen record of the slow transition of Remnant culture into something bizarre and almost alien.

It is here that they built their capital, in a deep valley that is almost always shrouded in clouds. In meadows farther up the mountain slopes, a few particularly hardy food crops are grown, but for the most part the Remnant rely on artificial greenhouses or cultured yeast for protein supplements. Remnant cuisine is unlikely to ever become a draw for tourists, even if their isolation here is broken.

description.text: Named after a mythical paradise, Shangri-La is an almost ideal planet, with a mixture of advanced, developed cities and uninhabited mountains. It is a rich and prosperous world, and nearly self-sufficient, but the cost of living here is prohibitively high for anyone from off-world. Because Polaris is on the very fringe of human space, and because of the wealth of its economy, piracy is a constant threat. Although recently the Syndicate has provided good protection, in past centuries it was not unheard of for raiding parties of starships to attack major port cities here, carrying off valuable cargo and sometimes also human slaves.

spaceport.text: The spaceport is state-of-the-art. So are the laser turrets and missile silos spaced out along its periphery. But somehow, instead of making you feel more secure, the defenses only serve to remind you of how far on the fringes of civilization you are, and of how rich this planet is compared to some of its neighbors. Everyone walking through the port is moving at a brisk, purposeful pace; loitering and sightseeing are not encouraged here.

missions.description: Remnant scouts report that the Korath are testing new warships at <waypoints>. Steal one and bring it back to <destination>. You may keep the ship after the Remnant study it.

values: Remnant scouts report that the Korath are testing new warships at <waypoints>. Steal one and bring it back to <destination>. You may keep the ship after the Remnant study it.

children.key: You see Taely at the cafeteria, but she's not eating. When she notices you, she waves you over. She signs, "Captain <last>, you are just the person I wanted to see!"
"Is there something you need from me?"
She looks at you in confusion. Before a misunderstanding can escalate, you explain that it was a joke.
She responds, "Sometimes the humor of ancient Earth is lost on me."
"Is there something you need from me?"

"While passing through <waypoints> a science team noted what looked like new warships being tested by the Korath." She shows you a picture. "Unfortunately they could not get more data without revealing their presence."

She signs, "I would like to suggest something more bold. Can you steal one and bring it back here? I want to get a close look at it. You can keep it once we are done studying it." A prototype Korath warship would be a nice catch. On the other hand, you have no idea how dangerous it is.
"I am not sure I want to take the risk."
You run into Taely at the spaceport. "<first> <last>! Have you reconsidered stealing one of those Korath warships we talked about?"
"I am still not sure I want to take the risk."
You find one of the new warships testing its weapons on asteroids while a Dredger collects the scraps. The warship turns to fight you!

values: You've captured the warship. Return to <destination> so Taely can examine it.

children.key: The Remnant run intensive scans on the unfamiliar ship as you approach the spaceport. Taely has a team of researchers ready to do a thorough inspection of the vessel as soon as you open the entry hatch. Their inspection is quick and efficient. After only a few hours they're done with the ship. "The level of automation is amazing," Taely signs. "The ship almost flies itself."

Will you avenge the fallen Remnant?

children.key: You locate the warehouse that was indicated in the message and land near it. On the way down, you notice several nearby hobos huddled by bonfires. It's difficult to see, but you are certain that they are armed with weapons.
You decide that the presence of the armed hobos is a risk you're unwilling to bear and abort the landing.

You make sure the gun at your hip is fully loaded before opening the cargo bay doors. A bald man in a gaudy suit waves at you and holds up a data pad. "Simply confirm payment on this data pad and it's all yours!"
"What, exactly, am I buying?" you ask.

"Behold!" he gestures towards the warehouse. As he speaks, the door to one of the docking bays slides open and inside is a shielding system. "The Infimum Shield Generator! Looted from a derelict Quarg vessel, it eventually found its way into our inventory."
By the time he finishes his sales pitch, a cargolift has positioned itself to load the bulky outfit onto your ship.
The salesman holds the data pad out expectantly.

He puts away the data pad. "Unfortunately, it appears we were unable to reach an agreement. Thank you for your time. However, I suggest you depart immediately." The armed hobos are no longer warming themselves by the fires and are instead trudging their way towards the warehouse. You decide to follow the man's suggestion.
"Congratulations on your purchase captain. I'm sure you won't regret it. You'll hear from us again if we happen to acquire any more unique  merchandise that might interest you."

children.key: A Remnant approaches you and signs, "Captain <last>, may I request your assistance?" Her face seems familiar. As you try to remember where you've seen her before she adds, "Thanks to your efforts, I was one of the fortunate ones to survive the destruction of our outpost on Baianus."

"My name is Ciconia. Before you were asked to intervene, I was supposed to retrieve the equipment from Baianus. But my ship, the Ancient Memory, was forced into a crash landing by the Korath. I would like to return to Baianus and salvage the ship, if possible."
"The Ancient Memory was probably obliterated during the attack."
"Can't you just get a new ship from the shipyard?"
"While I cannot deny that possibility, I still hold out hope that the wreckage is salvageable."
"The Ancient Memory was not just any ship. It was one of the last surviving Avialae, from the first generation in modern Remnant ship design! The Prefects halted production on them centuries ago."

She pauses to gather her thoughts then continues, "Unfortunately, my request to lead a salvage operation was denied by the Prefects. So now you are my last hope. Would you fly me to Baianus to search for the remains of the Ancient Memory?"
"Sorry, you will have to find some other way there."
"Thank you Captain <last>! May the Embers light our way."
"I am sorry for wasting your time." She walks away, dejected.

"Who was that Remnant on the Magpie?"
"What will you do once the Ancient Memory is repaired?"

Ciconia clenches her fist in frustration. "A Remnant Prefect who is a strong opponent of allowing large utility ships into the Remnant fleets. He, and others like him, are heavily in favor of dismantling them for spare parts whenever they are found. Your discovery of the Shattered Light only emboldened them to be more active."

Ciconia thinks a moment then signs, "If we rejoin the Remnant fleets once we are done here, I suspect we will not be allowed to keep the Ancient Memory. I hope you will not mind if we join you instead. The Avialae is an old ship, but I am sure it could prove to be a beneficial part of your fleet."
